result.name: acaps-humanitarian-access-dataset
result.notes:
ACAPS' Humanitarian Access Dataset compiles information on humanitarian access constraints across countries with active humanitarian crises. It is updated twice a year, each edition covering a six-month reporting period.
The dataset underpins the ACAPS Global Humanitarian Access Overview, which sets out how access to humanitarian assistance is restricted for crisis-affected populations worldwide.
Information is coded against three access pillars: access of people in need to aid; access of humanitarian actors to people in need; and physical, environmental, and security constraints. These are broken down into nine indicators and their sub-indicators. Indicators are scored from 0 to 3; pillars and the overall access score are expressed from 0 (no constraints) to 5 (extreme constraints), following the [ACAPS Humanitarian Access Methodology Note.](https://www.acaps.org/fileadmin/Technical_notes/20211207_acaps_humanitarian_access_methodology_note_december_2021.pdf)

The workbook contains:
About — an overview of the dataset and its methodology
pillars — pillar scores, the overall access score, the information gap, and the trend for each crisis, aggregated to country level
indicators — scores for each of the nine access indicators
trends — access scores across successive editions, showing change over time
dictionary — the data dictionary defining each variable
log — the coded entries, with sources and dates, reliability ratings, indicators and sub-indicators, and justifications
list — the master list of crises assessed, with ISO codes and crisis type
csv — a GIS-compatible summary with ISO codes

For more information, download the dataset. To access the ACAPS Global Humanitarian Access Overview, visit: https://www.acaps.org/en/thematics/all-topics/humanitarian-access-overview

organization.name: acaps
organization.title: ACAPS
organization.description:
We are an independent analytical voice helping humanitarian workers, influencers, fundraisers, and donors make better-informed decisions and respond more effectively to disasters.

We have no operational bias; we maintain editorial control based on the principle of impartiality.

We adapt to the circumstances and keep agility at the core of everything we do.

We are specialised in providing timely and independent needs analysis, data, training, and methodological tools targeting humanitarian decision-makers to ultimately help them respond more effectively to disasters

Our datasets are also available from an API system accessible at https://api.acaps.org/
